article_title: Using a computer simulation for teaching communication skills: A blinded multisite mixed methods randomized controlled trial
citation: Kron Frederick W. MD, Fetters Michael D. MD, MPH, MA, Scerbo Mark W. PhD, White Casey B. PhD, Lypson Monica L. MD, MHPE, FACP, Padilla Miguel A. PhD, Gliva-McConvey Gayle A., Belfore Lee A. II PhD, West Temple MPA, Wallace Amelia M. BM, Guetterman Timothy C. PhD, Schleicher Lauren S. MA, Kennedy Rebecca A. MS, Mangrulkar Rajesh S. MD, Cleary James F. MD, Marsella Stacy C. PhD, Becker Daniel M. MD. (2017). Using a computer simulation for teaching communication skills: A blinded multisite mixed methods randomized controlled trial. Patient Education and Counseling. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pec.2016.10.024
title: MPathic-VR virtual human conversation simulation for advanced healthcare communication training
description: MPathic-VR is a computer-based system in which healthcare learners "talk with virtual humans" — intelligent conversational agents with human appearance — in intercultural and interprofessional scenarios. Learners choose among three responses per exchange, are recorded for verbal and nonverbal behavior, receive a personalized after-action review with video of their nonverbal behaviors, and repeat each scenario. Analyses of learner data drive assessment, feedback, and real-time variation of virtual human behavior.
requirements: Built on specific communication skill learning objectives drawn from established protocols (SPIKES, CRASH, TeamSTEPPS), with a readiness assessment quiz requiring a score of 80% or higher before scenario participation.
constraints: The authors note MPathic-VR was more interactive by design and included two scenarios while assessment covered only the interprofessional content, so OSCE differences may reflect joint effects of content and delivery format.
target_learners: Healthcare learners training in advanced communication skills
examples: In the trial, students played an intern breaking bad news to a virtual mother about her daughter's leukemia, then resolving conflict with a virtual oncology nurse, with an after-action review between run-throughs.

article_title: Utilizing epigenetics to study the shared nature of development and biological aging across the lifespan
citation: Raffington, L. (2024). Utilizing epigenetics to study the shared nature of development and biological aging across the lifespan. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-024-00239-5
title: Generations of methylation profile scores as biomarkers of biological aging and related phenotypes
description: The article describes methylation profile scores (MPSs) computed from genome-wide DNA methylation, organized in generations: first-generation "epigenetic clocks" trained on chronological age that track it with correlation coefficients upwards of r = 0.95; second-generation measures (GrimAge, PhenoAge) trained on cross-sectional physiology and mortality; and third-generation measures such as DunedinPACE capturing longitudinal multisystem decline. Table 2 lists each measure's tissue, training criterion, and interpretation, including MPSs of inflammation, BMI, and Epigenetic-g for cognitive performance.
requirements: Genome-wide DNAm measurement technology and discovery samples large enough (thousands of individuals) to train predictive algorithms
constraints: Next-generation measures were developed in adult blood samples, so their cross-tissue and cross-age applicability must be considered
target_learning_goals: quantifying biological aging and cognitive performance as molecular readouts linking development and aging
examples: Table 2 lists DunedinPACE trained on 19 years of follow-up in 19 system-integrity biomarkers, interpreted as years of physiological decline per calendar year
key_sources: Raffington, L. (2024). Utilizing epigenetics to study the shared nature of development and biological aging across the lifespan. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-024-00239-5

article_title: Critical analysis of evidence about the impacts on surgical teams of 'mental practice' in systematic reviews: a systematic rapid evidence assessment (SREA).
citation: Snelgrove Huon; Gabbott Ben. (2020). Critical analysis of evidence about the impacts on surgical teams of ‘mental practice’ in systematic reviews: a systematic rapid evidence assessment (SREA). BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-02131-3
title: Adopt mental practice as an economical, sustainable addition to surgical training, including shared mental rehearsal within teams
description: The article concludes that in designing surgical training, team building and safety procedures, "MP has potential to improve performance and its application is highly economical, sustainable and feasible with current resources", offering an alternative to expensive technology-based simulation. It further proposes that teams can share their practical envisioning derived through MP to improve collective performance, positioning MP as an information-sharing practice proximal to the task and related to shared mental models, anticipatory thinking and situational awareness. Unlike reflective practice's retrospective review, MP privileges cultivating foresight.
requirements: Organisational support for MP resources, requiring organisational spaces, leadership and interpersonal expertise, for example instantiation in pre-surgical routines
constraints: The article states MP is still under theorised and little acknowledged, and that whether and how users apply MP post training remains largely unreported
examples: The article cites recent research suggesting teams can share mental rehearsals to improve collective performance, and describes MP embedded in warm-up routines of attention management, stress control and goal-setting.
key_sources: Snelgrove Huon; Gabbott Ben. (2020). Critical analysis of evidence about the impacts on surgical teams of ‘mental practice’ in systematic reviews: a systematic rapid evidence assessment (SREA). BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-02131-3

article_title: The Effect of Play Supported Program on the School Readiness of 60-72 Month-Old Disadvantaged Children
citation: Özgül Polat, Ayşegül Sönmez. (2015). The Effect of Play Supported Program on the School Readiness of 60-72 Month-Old Disadvantaged Children. TOJET: The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 14(3). https://www.tojet.net/
title: Marmara Primary Education Readiness Scale (MPERS)
description: A readiness measure developed and standardized by Polat Unutkan in 2003 for 60-78-month-old Turkish children, composed of a Development Form and an Application Form. The Development Form has "a total of 153 items" across cognitive and language, socio-emotional, physical development and self-care sub-scales and is filled out by teachers or parents; the Application Form is a 73-question pictorial test applied individually, with mathematics, science, sound, drawing and labyrinth sub-scales. Reported reliabilities include test-retest r=.99 (Development Form) and r=.93 (Application Form).
requirements: Development Form filled out by teachers or parents; Application Form applied individually to children
target_learning_goals: Primary school readiness measurement across developmental and applied skill domains
examples: Teachers filled out Development Forms and the researcher applied the Application Form to each child in this study
key_sources: Özgül Polat, Ayşegül Sönmez. (2015). The Effect of Play Supported Program on the School Readiness of 60-72 Month-Old Disadvantaged Children. TOJET: The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 14(3). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1067712

article_title: A Study of Developing Multicultural Awareness in Teacher Education: Watch, Write and Talk a Movie
citation: Karadeniz, O., & İncirci, A. (2016). A Study of Developing Multicultural Awareness in Teacher Education: Watch, Write and Talk a Movie. Journal of Education and Practice, 7(34), 81-89. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1119119
title: Multiculturalism Perception Scale (MPS)
description: A 25-item five-point Likert scale developed by Ayaz (2016) measuring multiculturalism perception, with response options from 1 (Totally Disagree) to 5 (Strongly Agree). Scores range from 25 to 125, with higher scores indicating higher multiculturalism perception. The scale contains only one negatively worded statement. Cronbach's Alpha was reported as 0.942 by Ayaz (2016) and 0.931 in this research.
requirements: Administered as pretest and posttest to measure perception change
constraints: Contains only one negative statement, which may affect response validity
examples: Used as pretest and posttest in this study with 61 trainee teachers
key_sources: Karadeniz, O., & İncirci, A. (2016). A Study of Developing Multicultural Awareness in Teacher Education: Watch, Write and Talk a Movie. Journal of Education and Practice, 7(34), 81-89. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1126694

article_title: Self-perceived competencies of Master of Public Health graduates and recommendations for programs in South Africa.
citation: Zweigenthal V, Christofides N, Dlungwane T, Matlala SF, Mokgatle MM, Opare A, Patrick SM, Schaay N, Shung-King M, Tshitangano T, Rispel L. (2026). Self-perceived competencies of Master of Public Health graduates and recommendations for programs in South Africa. PLOS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0360789
title: Eleven-domain, three-lens competency framework for assessing MPH graduate self-perceived competencies
description: The study adapted Zwanikken et al.'s validated LMIC instrument, adding items from prior South African MPH alumni studies and the investigators' experiential knowledge, yielding a self-administered questionnaire examining "58 self-perceived competencies in 11 domains", including public health sciences, health promotion, M&E, health policy, communication, context sensitivity, community and intersectoral skills, planning and management, crisis management, academic, and leadership. Competencies were assessed "through three lenses – their usefulness at work; perceptions whether they were obtained through MPH programs; and graduates’ confidence in their application", each scored on a four-item Likert scale and recoded to percentages of maximum domain scores.
requirements: Piloting for face validity; domain reliability checked with Cronbach alphas (0.72–0.95, except community and intersectoral below 0.7 for two lenses)
constraints: No nationally agreed competency set exists for South African MPH programs; M&E was made a separate domain for the South African public sector setting
examples: The tool was piloted among MPH graduates and alumni, after which project management, financial literacy and managing crises items were added
key_sources: Zweigenthal V, Christofides N, Dlungwane T, Matlala SF, Mokgatle MM, Opare A, Patrick SM, Schaay N, Shung-King M, Tshitangano T, Rispel L. (2026). Self-perceived competencies of Master of Public Health graduates and recommendations for programs in South Africa. PLOS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0360789

article_title: Simulation-based mastery learning for nasolacrimal duct probing in ophthalmology residency: a prospective pre-post educational study.
citation: Theerakulpisut Saralee, Tengtrisorn Supaporn, Singha Penny, Rattanalert Narisa. (2026). Simulation-based mastery learning for nasolacrimal duct probing in ophthalmology residency: a prospective pre–post educational study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09213-8
title: Multifaceted probing simulation (MPS) model: a low-cost rubber-and-silicone simulator head for nasolacrimal duct probing training
description: The MPS is a physical simulator head developed for nasolacrimal duct probing practice, costing 2,800 THB (approximately 80 USD) per model. The simulator head and nasal structures were fabricated from rubber to replicate external facial anatomy, with orbital soft tissue from soft silicone and the lacrimal drainage pathway simulated using silicone tubes commonly employed in dacryocystorhinostomy procedures. Rigid plastic plates represent bony structures, and the orbital section is detachable for easy replacement in the event of tube damage. The model was used for supervised practice, repeated self-directed practice, and video-recorded performance assessment.
requirements: The orbital section is detachable, allowing replacement when silicone tubes are damaged during practice
constraints: The simulator does not fully replicate the anatomical complexities of the human nasolacrimal system, such as duct resistance or the potential for false tract formation
examples: Used in a prospective pre–post study with 20 ophthalmology residents for supervised practice, self-directed practice, and video-based rubric assessment
key_sources: Theerakulpisut Saralee, Tengtrisorn Supaporn, Singha Penny, Rattanalert Narisa. (2026). Simulation-based mastery learning for nasolacrimal duct probing in ophthalmology residency: a prospective pre–post educational study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09213-8

article_title: Multicultural personality and effectiveness in an intercultural training simulation: The role of stress and pro-active communication.
citation: Hofhuis, J., Schilderman, M. F., & Verdooren, A. (2020). Multicultural personality and effectiveness in an intercultural training simulation: The role of stress and pro‐active communication. International Journal of Psychology, 55(5), 812–821. https://doi.org/10.1002/ijop.12647
title: Multicultural Personality Questionnaire (MPQ): five domain-specific traits for intercultural effectiveness
description: The MPQ (Van der Zee & Van Oudenhoven, 2001) is a domain-specific personality framework distinguishing five traits: Emotional Stability ("reflects the individuals ability to stay calm under novel and stressful conditions"), Flexibility, Openmindedness, Cultural Empathy, and Social Initiative ("a tendency to actively approach social situations, initiating communication rather than waiting and watching"). This study uses the 40-item short form to predict behaviour in simulated intercultural interaction.
requirements: Respondents self-report trait applicability; this study used the 40-item short form with five 8-item dimensions
constraints: Many MPQ items are not specifically formulated towards intercultural contexts and overlap with the Big Five
examples: Participants in five intercultural workshops completed the MPQ-SF several weeks before playing four rounds of Barnga
key_sources: Hofhuis, J., Schilderman, M. F., & Verdooren, A. (2020). Multicultural personality and effectiveness in an intercultural training simulation: The role of stress and pro‐active communication. International Journal of Psychology, 55(5), 812–821. https://doi.org/10.1002/ijop.12647
